title: Two approved rules, now for Camps: the trash icon (R5-03) and the one offline bar (C19)
subtitle: Real preview screens of the built app with each change tried. Nothing new is invented here: both rules are already in the rulebook (v1.048 (22) and v0.626: every family page removes a child with the gray trash icon button; v1.005 and v1.123: one offline bar for the whole dashboard, and Camps' own refresh bar folds into it). This picture only shows how they look on Camps' two screens. Amber = what differs.

sections.heading: 1 · The family sign-up page: removing child 2 or 3 (R5-03)

columns.label: Today

row.caption: PC: “Remove” is a blue underlined word (never drawn in a mockup).

columns.note: Forms' family page, the kiosk and Fill in already use the trash icon (v0.626).

columns.label: After

row.caption: PC: the 28 px gray trash icon button; its name “Remove child 2” shows as a dark tooltip on hover and keyboard focus (shown here).
Touch (820, 390, 320): the same icon with a 44 px tap area. Removing works as before.

columns.note: The same card is Fill in's child card in the dashboard, which already has the shared icon button.

sections.heading: 2 · The camp page when the roster keeps failing to refresh (C19)

items.caption: PC, after two failed reloads (about 30 seconds): two amber bars — the shared “You’re offline” bar on top and Camps' own “Couldn’t refresh the roster” bar with Retry.

columns.label: After

items.caption: PC: only the shared bar. It has no button and goes away by itself when the connection is back.
Phone: the same one bar; the page below starts higher.

columns.note: “Updated 12:00:07 AM” above the count cards stays (v1.014). The roster reloads by itself every 15 seconds and at once when the browser says it is back online.

footer: What goes: Camps' own bar and its Retry (v0.718's “Couldn’t refresh the roster. Check the connection, then retry.”), and the word “Remove” on the family page. What stays: every save's own amber bar (a failed Mark paid still has its Retry), the shared offline bar's words, and the roster's “Updated …” line. No database change.
